title: Symmetric Tree Mirror Inversion Check
statement_md:
Given the `root` of a binary tree represented as a level-order array, check whether it is a mirror of itself (i.e., symmetric around its center).

### Input Format
- A JSON-encoded list representing the level-order binary tree `root`

### Output Format
- A boolean value (`true` or `false`)

examples.explanation: Left and right subtrees are mirror reflections of each other.

hints.text: Two trees are mirrors if their roots have the same value and each tree's right child mirrors the other's left child.
Write a helper isMirror(t1, t2) comparing t1.left with t2.right and t1.right with t2.left.
Use Tree Traversal with simultaneous dual-node recursion.

editorial_md:
### Optimal Approach: Dual-Node Mirror Traversal

Define `isMirror(n1, n2)`. Both null -> true. One null -> false. Check `n1.val == n2.val` and recursively verify `isMirror(n1.left, n2.right)` and `isMirror(n1.right, n2.left)`.

#### Complexity
- **Time Complexity:** $O(n)$ all nodes examined once.
- **Space Complexity:** $O(h)$ tree height recursion stack.

#### Common Pitfalls
- Comparing `n1.left` with `n2.left` instead of `n2.right`.
